messages.author: da509bd8f2d340da
messages.subject: INLA program crashed on HPC
parts:
Hi,

I was trying to run INLA on a spatiotemporal dataset on a node of high performance computing cluster.

The dataset has ~5000 points with 24 time stamps, and I roughly followed the codes of Cameletti et al. 2012.
The computing node has 24 cores and 64G memory running a centOS, and I used  INLA:::inla.dynload.workaround() 
to get INLA running.  INLA rashed immediately when trying to run function of inla().  Please see the following for
the message. Is 64G of memory not enough for this model?  It seems INLA crashed before even started to allocate memory.

Thanks much for the help.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA program crashed on HPC
parts:
On Sun, 2016-11-06 at 14:04 -0800, surf wrote:
> Hi, 
>
> I was trying to run INLA on a spatiotemporal dataset on a node of
> high performance computing cluster. 
>
> The dataset has ~5000 points with 24 time stamps, and I roughly
> followed the codes of Cameletti et al. 2012. 
> The computing node has 24 cores and 64G memory running a centOS, and
> I used  INLA:::inla.dynload.workaround()  
> to get INLA running.  INLA rashed immediately when trying to run
> function of inla().  Please see the following for 
> the message. Is 64G of memory not enough for this model?  It seems
> INLA crashed before even started to allocate memory.
>

can you try to set some parameters to reduce the memory usage, like

inla(..., control.inla=list(int.strategy = "eb", strategy="gaussian"),
num.threads=2)

and see if that one runs. otherwise, try to reduce the number of
timesteps. 

if this runs then the mem-usage is the issue. 

with 24cores and (only) 64Gb mem, then you need to reduce the number of
cores, as its the memory pr used core that is important. 

H
--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA program crashed on HPC
parts:
Thanks for the response, Dr. Rue. I used the control.inla parameters you suggested and tried
different number of time steps.  It worked for 6 time steps with no problems, but still crashed
for 12 steps. For 6 number of time steps, INLA actually only used 5G of memory at peak, should it
use (2^2)*5 = 20G for 12 steps?  Not sure why it cannot finish for 12.
